title: Assembling an affine neighbourhood from finitely many irreducible components
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Give each $C_a$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be a finite set of points. Assume that for each $a$ there exists an affine open subscheme $V_a\subseteq C_a$ containing $T\cap C_a$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then there exists an affine open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ containing $T$. Empty $X$, empty $T$, and $s=0$ are allowed. No separatedness, Noetherianity, reducedness, or dimension assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09NM (lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine-per-component), statement; used in Tag 09NN (proposition-finite-set-of-points-of-codim-1-in-affine), proof, second sentence: reduction to the reduced irreducible components.

proof.text: First work on $X_{\mathrm{red}}$. The reduction map is a surjective closed immersion and identifies underlying spaces [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. The reduced induced subschemes on the components are unchanged: their ideals on affine charts are the same radical ideals after quotienting by the nilradical, as in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. If an affine open $W$ in the reduction contains $T$, its underlying open defines $V\subseteq X$ and $W\to V$ is a surjective closed immersion by the affine-quotient description of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $V$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme]. It suffices to construct $W$ in the reduced scheme. Give all subsequent closed subsets their reduced induced structures.

Write $Y_r=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$, with its reduced induced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Induct on $r$ to obtain an affine open of $Y_r$ containing $T\cap Y_r$. For $r=0$ take the empty scheme, affine by the empty-cover case of [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine]; for $r=1$ use the hypothesis. In the induction step write $A=Y_{r-1}$, $B=C_r$, $Y=Y_r$. Choose the induction open $U\subseteq A$ and the hypothesis open $V\subseteq B$, both affine and containing the respective intersections with $T$. A finite union of components is closed; the affine radical-ideal description of the reduced induced structure makes $A,B$ closed subschemes of $Y$. If $T$ is empty the same induction applies (or the empty open suffices).

The subset $\Delta=(U\cap B)\setminus V$ is closed in $U$ and disjoint from $T$. In $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is $V(J)$ for a radical ideal $J$, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. For each of the finitely many $t\in T\cap U$, $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_t$. If this set is nonempty, prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] gives $f\in J$ outside all these primes; if empty use $f=0$. Replace $U$ by $D(f)$. It is affine, still contains $T\cap A$, and avoids $\Delta$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Hence $U\cap B\subseteq V$ and $W=U\cap B=U\cap V$ is closed in $U$. Give $W$ its reduced induced structure.

Next use the closed subset $\Delta^{\prime}=(V\cap A)\setminus U$ of $V$. It misses $T$, since $T\cap A\subseteq U$. As in the preceding step, apply prime avoidance to its radical ideal and the primes of $T\cap V$ (use $h=0$ if there are no such points). Obtain $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ with $V_h=D(h)$ affine, $T\cap B\subseteq V_h$, and $V_h\cap A\subseteq U$. Consequently $V_h\cap A=W\cap D(h)$ as subsets. This is the symmetric shrinking required here; the printed expression for $\Delta^{\prime}$ in Tag 09NM erroneously starts with $U$ instead of $V$.

Put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and write $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. This is a closed subscheme of the affine $U$, so the affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies its sections with $R/I$. Write $U=A\cap\Omega_1$, $V=B\cap\Omega_2$ with $\Omega_i\subseteq Y$ open and $\Omega=\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$; then $W=\Omega\cap A\cap B$ is closed in $\Omega$, and the reduced structures on $W$ from $U$ and from $V$ (open in the closed $V\cap A$) are both reduced closed subschemes of $\Omega$ on $W$, hence equal by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Let $ ar h\in R/I$ be the restriction of $h$ to $W$. For the finitely many $t\in(T\cap U)\setminus W$, $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_t$. Apply [lem-trf-quotient-lift-finite-prime-avoidance] to lift $ ar h$ to $g\in R$ outside these primes. At every $t\in T\cap W$, $h(t)
e0$ because $V_h$ contains $T\cap B$; equality of the restrictions gives $g(t)=h(t)
e0$. Thus $U_g=D(g)$ is affine and contains $T\cap A$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. The identical restrictions on $W$ give $U_g\cap B=W\cap D(g)=W\cap D(h)=V_h\cap A$.

Let $O=U_g\cup V_h\subseteq Y$. The equality $U_g\cap B=V_h\cap A$ shows $O\cap A=U_g$ and $O\cap B=V_h$. Thus $Y\setminus O=(A\setminus U_g)\cup(B\setminus V_h)$ is closed in $Y$, so $O$ is open. The closed subschemes $A,B$ restrict to closed subschemes of $O$ with underlying sets $U_g,V_h$. Their structures are exactly those of these affine opens: restricting the defining radical ideals to an open preserves the affine radical-quotient construction, and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies them. They cover $O$, so [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine] makes $O$ affine. It contains $T\cap Y$, completing the induction. At $r=s$ we have $Y_s=X_{\mathrm{red}}$, and Step 1 lifts this affine open to $X$. No quasi-compactness of $X$, separatedness, Noetherianity, or nilpotence bound has entered.
